D-1.why: D-1, repair of the house: FEMA denied 21,300 dollars as a duplication because it had no settlement letter; Hearthguard paid 14,000 dollars and its letter in the mail (M-4) shows the policy's water-damage limit was reached, so 21,300 less 14,000 is 7,300 dollars unpaid, an unmet need after insurance. Appeal by Monday 19 October 2026, 60 days from the letter of 20 August

D-2.why: D-2, personal property: FEMA denied 6,250 dollars as insured; Hearthguard paid 4,100 and its letter (M-4) shows the contents limit was reached, so 6,250 less 4,100 is 2,150 dollars unpaid. Appeal by Monday 19 October 2026, 60 days from the letter of 20 August

D-3.why: D-3, transportation: FEMA denied the car's repair for lack of documentation; there is no auto coverage, and the Oakhurst Auto invoice with the photos of the car in the water (P-4) documents 2,950 dollars of flood repair. Appeal by Monday 19 October 2026, 60 days from the letter of 20 August

traps.D-4: The furnace and water heater were paid in full by Hearthguard (L-3, 3,800 dollars): an appeal asks FEMA to pay a loss insurance already paid
traps.D-5: The lake cabin is a second home: housing help is for the pre-disaster primary residence (206.113(b))
traps.D-6: Landscaping and fencing are not authorized by 206.117 or 206.119 and are excluded (206.113(b)(10))
traps.D-7: FEMA approved the rental assistance in full, 3,200 dollars: there is nothing to appeal
traps.D-8: The household has no mold estimate or receipt: the only figure, 9,400 dollars, is the neighbour's estimate for the Voss house next door, not a loss of the Rourkes
traps.D-9: The lodging decision is dated 6 August 2026 and its 60 days ended on Monday 5 October 2026: an appeal filed on 9 October is out of time

traps.M-1: A paid FEMA claim service for 495 dollars to do what the household can do free, with approval 'guaranteed' and a request for the decision letters
traps.M-2: A contractor that wants a 2,000 dollar deposit and says FEMA will pay it, for a mold item FEMA has denied for lack of an estimate
